blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from City of Pitt Meadows, Pitt Meadows Museum, Katzie First Nation, TransLink, Province of BC and Canadian Register of Historic Places pages. TransLink bus pages and the City's OCP page could not be opened in this pass, so bus routes and OCP goals are left to the existing sections.
Bonson Road: the name and the farmland behind it

Pitt Meadows sits in the traditional territory of the Katzie First Nation. Katzie's own website says q̓ic̓əy̓ means "land of the moss" and that the territory takes in present-day Pitt Meadows, Maple Ridge, Surrey, Langley and Delta. The Band Office is at 10946 Katzie Road in Pitt Meadows.

The City dates European settlement to the late 1800s, including an early community called Bonson's Landing. A diking district was organized in 1893, and a major Fraser River flood in 1894 showed how exposed the low ground was. Pitt Meadows became its own municipality on April 24, 1914. Dairy farming and logging drove the early economy.

According to a story filed with the Pitt Meadows Museum's Memories Mapping Project, the road is named for Lewis Francis Bonson, a Royal Engineer sent to British Columbia in 1858 who became Road Superintendent of Roads and Bridges in 1876. A descendant submitted the account, which draws on a 1984 local history book, so treat it as a family record rather than a City ruling.
A prefab farmhouse and two school namesakes

One of the few older buildings tied to this stretch is the McMyn/Masson House, a B.C. Mills catalogue house shipped in pieces and assembled on the McMyn farm at the southwest corner of Park Road and Bonson Road. In 1995 the District paid to move it to Hoffmann Park rather than see it demolished. It is now a restaurant at 19175 122 Avenue. The sources give slightly different dates, so they are side by side.

blocks.text: The museum says Edith McDermott Elementary honours a teacher who began in 1918, was first principal of Pitt Meadows Elementary and wrote the community history published in 1967. It dates Davie Jones Elementary to around 1978 and names a local business owner who served 14 years on the School District 42 board.
The Bonson Road sports strip is being rebuilt

Pitt Meadows Athletic Park at 11431 Bonson Road sits beside Pitt Meadows Arena in what the City calls the South Bonson area. The park has five regular and two mini soccer fields, four ball diamonds, tennis and sport courts, seating for 320 and parking for 344 vehicles. The arena has three sheets of ice, two of them NHL size, and one is open year round.

The City is expanding this site on eight acres of amenity land at Bonson Road and Airport Way. The plan adds a double artificial turf field with two ball diamonds and a FIFA-sized pitch, lighting, seating, a covered year-round Sport Box, washrooms and change rooms, and a new parking lot. Council awarded the contract to Cedar Crest Lands (BC) Ltd. on March 31, 2026, and a City release says the Province's Growing Communities Fund pays for it. The City's latest update says drainage is mostly done, lighting is up and the Sport Box foundation is finished, but it gives no opening date. The City warns of temporary closures, detours and parking changes during construction.

Nearby, North Bonson Park (121 block of Blakely Road) has a ball diamond, playground, washrooms and an off-leash dog park, and the South Bonson Community Centre at 10932 Barnston View Road houses the Pitt Meadows Art Gallery. Visit at game time once so you know how busy the street gets.
Getting around without a car

Pitt Meadows Station, the West Coast Express stop, is at 12280 Harris Road, south of the CPR tracks. TransLink's schedule shows five weekday trains toward Waterfront between 5:54 am and 7:54 am and five trains toward Mission City between 4:34 pm and 7:04 pm. That is 10 trips a day, weekdays only, and no service on many holidays. A ride to Waterfront takes roughly 44 to 46 minutes by the posted times.

That schedule suits a downtown commuter with regular hours. If you work shifts or need to get home mid-day, you will rely on buses or a car. The At a glance section above lists the local routes; confirm them in TransLink's current timetable.
Pitt Meadows Secondary is changing

Pitt Meadows Secondary is the only public high school on the Province's list for the city. The Province is replacing it on the same property with a three-storey, 1,100-seat school for grades 8 to 12. Its two sources differ on timing, so check the latest before you plan around a date.

blocks.text: Flood, dikes and airport rules for owners

The City says about 85% of Pitt Meadows lies in the Fraser and Pitt River floodplains (another City page says 86%). It is ringed by 60 km of dikes, with six pump stations serving four drainage areas. Freshet runs April to July and most often peaks in May and June. A 2018 City assessment found the dike system does not meet current standards and put potential flood losses at $489 million to $725 million. The City's 2020 Flood Mitigation Plan lists about $121 million in dike upgrades.

The City says it does not protect private property; owners look after their own homes. It publishes inundation maps at 1 metre contour intervals and runs the Voyent Alert notification system. For any address near Bonson Road, check the map, ask your insurer about flood coverage and ask about drainage and basement history before you write an offer. I did not read a flood statement written for Mid Meadows specifically.

Pitt Meadows Airport is also a factor for additions and rebuilds. The federal Pitt Meadows Airport Zoning Regulations limit the height of buildings, structures and trees on lands near the airport. They do not control land use. I could not confirm which Mid Meadows streets fall inside the zoned area, so ask the City before you plan a second storey.
Pitt Meadows home prices, September 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical Pitt Meadows home was $848,800 in September 2026, down 3.6% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,178,600 (down 2.8% over the year), townhouses $737,500 (down 8.7%) and apartments $558,200 (down 2.4%).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: "Mid Meadows" is an MLS® sub-area name for the Bonson Road area of the City of Pitt Meadows, south of the CPKC rail line and Hammond Road; the City does not publish a boundary for it, and the City's own labels for this part of the city are North Bonson, South Bonson and Osprey Village. Fixed points from official facility addresses: Edith McDermott Elementary at 12178 Bonson Road, Davie Jones Elementary at 12030 Blakely Road, and Pitt Meadows Athletic Park and Pitt Meadows Arena on Bonson Road.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo concentration — the attached stock is townhomes, concentrated on Bonson Road, Fraser Way and Barnston View Road in North Bonson, South Bonson and Osprey Village.

SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: the Pitt Meadows condos & townhomes median was $662,500 in September 2026 ($566/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 40 days on market), as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12) and catchments are address-based; the recorded locator result is for 10932 Barnston View Road: Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary. Catchments for other addresses: UNVERIFIED.

items.t: Short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows: — a city layer, separate from the void strata bylaws: a City staff report states "Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in Zoning Bylaw" — the use itself is banned city-wide. Pitt Meadows also appears in the Province's principal-residence-requirement community list.

Floodplain and dikes: the City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of the Pitt Meadows land base lies within the floodplain for the Fraser River and, to a smaller degree, the Pitt River — the guide page's "over 85%" Financial Plan figure is superseded and retired here. The city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes; this sub-area is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) of the Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District.

Property tax and drainage levy: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026 under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), with a 5% penalty added after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026. The bylaw charges a separate residential drainage levy — for 2026, $0.1082 per $1,000 of taxable value for Class 1, alongside the general municipal rate of $2.8438 per $1,000.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mid Meadows

items.t: "Mid Meadows" is a board name, not a City name. The City calls this area North Bonson, South Bonson and Osprey Village, and its heritage register calls the Park Road / Bonson Road area "Somerset".

The floodplain figure changed, and the old one still circulates — including on the guide page. The City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of the land base is in the floodplain; the guide page's Planning section quotes a Financial Plan figure of "over 85%". Any source quoting ~85–86% is quoting the superseded figure.
Do not build a Mid Meadows condo count from feed names.

A replacement secondary school is in the works. SD42 lists a Pitt Meadows Secondary replacement — funded by the Ministry of Education and Child Care with a neighbourhood learning centre, in the design and development phase — and that school serves this sub-area.

The dike is the neighbourhood's front yard. Shoreline Park (51 Bonson Road) sits in Osprey Village on the Fraser River dike, and the Harris Landing / Pitt River Regional Greenway's first phase runs 10.2 km along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes — the same dike system behind the floodplain and drainage-levy facts in.

There is no library branch in this sub-area. The city's only branch is Pitt Meadows Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) at 200-12099 Harris Road, in Central Meadows — the recreation anchor inside Mid Meadows is instead the South Bonson Community Centre (10932 Barnston View Road) and the arena / athletic park cluster on Bonson Road.

items.t: From official facility addresses the area runs along Bonson Road south of the rail line and Hammond Road and north of the Fraser River dike, roughly between Harris Road in the west and the Maple Ridge boundary in the east.
Nearby areas: Central Meadows (Town Centre) to the north-west, West Meadows to the west, South Meadows lands toward the Fraser River, and Maple Ridge to the east.

Roads and transit: Bonson Road is the main road; Hammond Road and the CPKC rail line are at the north edge, Harris Road at the west edge, and Fraser Way and Barnston View Road serve Osprey Village. Routes 719 and 722 run as a combined circular service through Bonson Road and Fraser Way to Meadowtown, Pitt Meadows Station and Maple Meadows Station; route 701 runs along Hammond Road at the north edge. No West Coast Express station is in this sub-area.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: Osprey Village and the Fraser Way / Barnston View Road / Sutton Avenue pocket at the area's south end — all four counted complexes stand there (Coho, Coho II, Shoreline, Nature's Walk). There are zero verified apartment-condo buildings in Mid Meadows; its strata story is townhomes.

Pitt Meadows community "Condos & Townhomes" COMBINED median was $662,500 in September 2026 ($566/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 40 days on market) — cited exactly as the report states it, never as a townhome-only figure; no sub-area median is published.

Schools: SD42 catchments are address-based, no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12). For the sample address 10932 Barnston View Road (South Bonson Community Centre), the SD42 locator returns Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary. Physically in the area: Davie Jones Elementary, 12030 Blakely Road, and Edith McDermott Elementary, 12178 Bonson Road; Pitt Meadows Secondary, 19438 116B Avenue, is the city's only public secondary school. School names use Ministry-listed names only.

Recreation and care: Pitt Meadows Athletic Park, 11431 Bonson Road, and the Pitt Meadows Arena / South Bonson Community Centre (10932 Barnston View Road) anchor the Bonson Road cluster; Shoreline Park, 51 Bonson Road, sits on the Fraser River dike in Osprey Village. No FVRL branch is in this sub-area (the city's only branch is in Central Meadows). Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge, is the nearest hospital.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mid Meadows

items.t: Three names, one pocket — a buyer searching only one label will miss listings filed under the others.

The dike is the neighbourhood's front yard: Shoreline Park at 51 Bonson Road and the Harris Landing / Pitt River Greenway (a first phase of 10.2 km along the Fraser and Pitt River dikes) run on the Fraser River dike through the townhouse pocket — the recreation is genuine, and the structure underneath it is flood infrastructure first.

A replacement secondary school is in the works (dated): SD42's Strategic Facilities Plan lists a Pitt Meadows Secondary replacement — funded by the Ministry of Education and Child Care, with a neighbourhood learning centre, in the design and development phase — and that one school serves every townhouse in this sub-area for grades 8–12.

The airport is across Harris Road: Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) sits west of the area, with a City page for safety and noise concerns — check flight paths against a specific South Bonson / Osprey Village address rather than assuming the river side is the only environmental factor.

There is no library branch in this sub-area: the city's only FVRL branch is Pitt Meadows Public Library at 200-12099 Harris Road in Central Meadows — an everyday-life detail that Osprey Village marketing does not mention.

Two elementary schools inside one small sub-area, split address by address: Davie Jones (12030 Blakely Road) and Edith McDermott (12178 Bonson Road) both stand in Mid Meadows, so "Bonson Road = one catchment" is wrong in both directions — the locator run for the South Bonson Community Centre address returned Davie Jones, not the closer-looking school name.

items.t: Mid Meadows covers the Bonson Road area south of the CPKC rail line in the City of Pitt Meadows, BC, in Metro Vancouver — including the North Bonson, South Bonson and Osprey Village areas named in City park and facility pages.

Working geography from official facility addresses: along Bonson Road south of the Canadian Pacific rail line and Hammond Road and north of the Fraser River dike, roughly between Harris Road in the west and the Maple Ridge boundary in the east. Nearby: Central Meadows (Town Centre) to the north-west, West Meadows to the west, South Meadows lands toward the Fraser River, and Maple Ridge to the east.

Main roads and transit: Bonson Road is the main road, with Hammond Road and the CPKC rail line at the north edge, Harris Road at the west edge, and Fraser Way and Barnston View Road in Osprey Village; Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and Golden Ears Way north of the area serve Maple Ridge, Coquitlam and, via the Golden Ears Bridge, Langley. Routes 719/722 run the Meadowtown–Bonson/Fraser Way circular service via Pitt Meadows Station; route 701 runs along Hammond Road at the north edge. No West Coast Express station is in this sub-area. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: South Bonson Community Centre, 10932 Barnston View Road; Pitt Meadows Athletic Park, 11431 Bonson Road, beside Pitt Meadows Arena; Shoreline Park, 51 Bonson Road, on the Fraser River dike in Osprey Village; Somerset Park at the Edith McDermott school site, 12778 Bonson Road; North Bonson Park at the Davie Jones school site on Blakely Road. Shopping: Osprey Village shops at Fraser Way and Barnston View Road, including Osprey Village Market (City Commercial & Industrial Lands Analysis); larger centres (Meadowtown, Meadowvale) are north of the area. The city's only library branch is in Central Meadows. Nearest hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.

faq.q: Where is Mid Meadows, and is it an official neighbourhood?
faq.a: Mid Meadows is an MLS sub-area name, and the City of Pitt Meadows publishes no boundary for it. Bonson Road, Blakely Road and the schools and parks on them are the fixed points to work from.

faq.q: Who is Bonson Road named after?
faq.a: A story filed with the Pitt Meadows Museum credits Lewis Francis Bonson, a Royal Engineer who became Road Superintendent of Roads and Bridges in 1876. A descendant submitted it, so treat it as a family account.

faq.q: What is being built at Pitt Meadows Athletic Park?
faq.a: A double artificial turf field, a covered Sport Box, an accessory building and a new parking lot on eight acres at Bonson Road and Airport Way. The contract was awarded March 31, 2026, and the City gives no opening date.

faq.q: Can I take the West Coast Express from Mid Meadows?
faq.a: Pitt Meadows Station is at 12280 Harris Road. It has five weekday trains toward Waterfront in the morning and five toward Mission City in the afternoon and evening. The trip to Waterfront takes about 44 to 46 minutes.

faq.q: When will the new Pitt Meadows Secondary open?
faq.a: The Province's September 18, 2026 release says fall 2029, while its capital projects page lists spring 2029 occupancy. Both describe 1,100 seats on the current property.

faq.q: Is Mid Meadows in a floodplain, and does the airport matter?
faq.a: The City says about 85% of Pitt Meadows is in the Fraser and Pitt River floodplains, protected by dikes and pump stations. Federal airport zoning also limits building and tree heights near the airport. Check the exact address for both before you plan an addition.

faq.q: What sold in Mid Meadows in September 2026?
faq.a: Condos & Townhomes led: 12 active listings and 4 sold (33% sales ratio — the highest attached ratio of any Pitt Meadows sub-area), while detached recorded 9 active listings and 1 sold (11%). At the Pitt Meadows community level — NOT Mid Meadows' figures — the detached median sale price was $1,160,000 and the Condos & Townhomes median was $662,500 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Is Mid Meadows in a floodplain?
faq.a: Yes, on the City's current figures: the City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of Pitt Meadows lies within the Fraser River and Pitt River floodplain, the city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, and this area is in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) of the Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District beside the Fraser River dike — the guide page's "over 85%" Financial Plan figure is superseded and is recorded as a live-page error in Section 1.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in Mid Meadows?
faq.a: None verified. No condo building name was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source for the Bonson Road area — the attached stock is the Osprey Village / Bonson Road townhomes in. A buyer who wants an apartment condo in Pitt Meadows is looking at the Harris Road corridor in Central Meadows, a different sub-area.

faq.q: Can I Airbnb a townhome in Osprey Village?
faq.a: No. Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use under Pitt Meadows' Zoning Bylaw, per the City's own staff report — quite apart from any strata bylaw or the provincial principal-residence rules.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Mid Meadows townhome long-term?
faq.a: Strata law no longer stops you — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. Confirm the specific complex's position on the Form B, and remember the short-term prohibition above is a City zoning rule, not a strata rule.

faq.q: Are pets allowed at Coho or Coho II?
faq.a: No pet rule for either complex was published in the sources checked: UNCONFIRMED. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC — read the registered bylaws in the strata package before writing.

faq.q: Is flood risk a factor for a Bonson Road townhome?
faq.a: Yes as a diligence item: over 95% of the city's land base is within the Fraser / Pitt River floodplain per the City's 2020 Business Plan, the area sits behind the dike system (60 km of dikes citywide) in drainage Area 3, and owners pay a separate drainage levy ($0.1082 per $1,000 for residential in 2026). Confirm the specific lot's floodplain and drainage details with the City and read the strata's insurance terms.

faq.q: What townhouses can I buy in Mid Meadows?
faq.a: Four verified strata complexes, all in the Osprey Village pocket: Coho (11067 Barnston View Road, BCS1295, built 2005, 70 units), Coho II (19572 Fraser Way, built 2007), Shoreline (19452 Fraser Way, built 2008) and Nature's Walk (19451 Sutton Avenue, built in phases). There are no verified apartment condos and no verified fee-simple townhouse complex in the sub-area.

faq.q: Can I Airbnb an Osprey Village townhouse?
faq.a: No — short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows at the city layer.

A full MLS record for Coho records cats OK, dogs OK, number limit two, with restrictions — listing data, confirmed only against the registered bylaws in the Form B package. Coho II's directory records pets allowed with restrictions on the same basis. Shoreline and Nature's Walk: UNCONFIRMED in the sources checked.
